newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan awaits U.S. request to shelter Hamas leader.
newsitem.headline: Jordan awaits U.S. request to shelter Hamas leader.

text.p: Jordan's Foreign Minister Fayez al-Tarawneh said on Sunday his government was still waiting for the United States to request formally that it give shelter to a jailed political leader of the militant Islamic group Hamas.

Tarawneh said Jordan, which expelled former Hamas politburo chief Mousa Abu Marzook two years ago under pressure from Washington, Israel and the Palestinians, would not let Abu Marzook back without an explicit U.S. request.
"There should be a written request. I think it will (come) very soon," he told journalists.

Abu Marzook, accused by Israel of responsibility for a wave of attacks in which scores of Israelis died, was arrested in New York a few weeks after his expulsion from Jordan in 1995. He was jailed while Israel sought his extradition, but was not charged.

Security officials said in February that Israel, fearing a wave of violence if he were extradited to an Israeli prison, would drop its demand for Abu Marzook's extradition in return for a pledge by him to shun violence.
Jordan said last week King Hussein would allow him to return "without any obligations" other than abiding by Jordanian law.
"It is unconditional. It is a deportation not an extradition. We are not taking him into custody," Tarawneh said, adding that Abu Marzook could return to Jordan next week.
"The information that I have is that he will come within four or five days. But the exact time -- the United States didn't even tell his family," Hamas representative in Jordan Mohammad Nazzal said.
"He will not sign any conditions," Nazzal added. Hamas officials have said Abu Marzook would play a "leading role" in the organisation if he returned to Amman.
Abu Marzook has maintained throughout his detention that he was only involved in political activities while in Amman.

Suicide bombers from the military wing of Hamas, which rejects Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's self-rule deal with Israel as a sell-out, killed dozens of Israelis in a series of attacks one year ago.
Jordan, which has in the past had uneasy relations with Arafat, appeared to have distanced itself from Hamas and moved more solidly behind the Palestinian leader after the expulsion of Abu Marzook.

But last month Jordan's Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali met Amman-based Hamas politburo chief Khaled Meshal, who took over from Abu Marzook after his imprisonment, in what Hamas said was the highest level meeting for over two years.
